eligibility: rated standard-chess win in 2026 (both sites, no Chess.com coach/bot games, no variants)
excluded: opponent berserked (Lichess WhiteBerserk/BlackBerserk header, or opponent started with under 60% of the base clock); this removes the +560 win (the opponent berserked)
excluded: abandonments; wins on time before move 20; any game under 20 moves; Lichess opponents on the provisional 1500 default

excluded: any game where he made a blunder: an engine "Blunder" judgment, or any of his moves where the eval swung 2.00+ pawns against him (mate capped at ±10). Comeback-from-a-blunder wins therefore do not qualify

requires per-move engine data, so blunder-free play can be verified (Chess.com Aug 2–Oct 1 and Oct 26–Nov 21 2026 via local Stockfish, plus Chess.com Game Review where it exists; Lichess server-analysed games)
data_note: This week (Nov 16–22): 410 rated Chess.com games, 189 wins, 190 losses, 31 draws. Bullet hit a new high of 1763 on Nov 17 and closed the week at 1702; blitz finished at 1465. Chess.com data through Nov 21, 2026 (489 new games since the Nov 13 refresh: Nov 13–21). No Lichess games since Sep 23.

week.label: Game of the Week
week.window: 2026-11-17 → 2026-11-23 ET (week in progress; games through Nov 21)
week.window_note: Chess.com only (no Lichess games since Sep 23). 17 of the 157 wins of 20+ moves were blunder-free on our Stockfish pass and Chess.com Game Review.

winner.caption: 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1549, out of 1.e3. 21...Qf2 forced the queens off, and after 22.Qxf2 Rxf2 his rook went hunting: 28...Rxd2+ took a knight, 30...Rxg1+ the other one and 31...Rxa1 the rook. His g-pawn queened on move 51 and 62...Ra5# finished it. No blunders on Chess.com Game Review (81.7 accuracy) and 3.7s left on his clock.
winner.why: Highest score (67.6) of the 17 blunder-free wins from Nov 17 to Nov 22, and the highest-scoring win of November. A real game: his eval only stayed above +3.00 for good from move 21, and he converted the queenless middlegame all the way to mate.

runner_up.caption: 1-minute bullet as White against a 1619, out of the Polish (1.b4). Level for twenty moves, then 22.Bg4 offered the bishop. 22...Nxg4 took it but pulled the f6 knight off the long diagonal, and 23.Qxg7# was mate with the b2 bishop behind the queen. No blunders on Chess.com Game Review (87.1 accuracy) and 22.4s left on his clock.
runner_up.why: Second of the 17 blunder-free wins that week (62.7), against a higher-rated opponent. The game was level until the 22.Bg4 trap, so the win came from a real contest rather than an early slip.

month.label: Game of the Month
month.window_note: 60 blunder-free wins from Nov 2 to Nov 21. The top-scoring November game (Nov 17, 67.6) is the Game of the Week, so it is not repeated here.

winner.caption: 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1405, out of 1.d4 c5. 12...Bxa1 won the exchange, the queens came off, and his rooks took over the second rank: 26...Rxf2+ started a chase that drove the king to d1, 33...Rgxc2 collected the knight and 36...Ra1# finished it. 93.3 accuracy on Chess.com Game Review, no blunders and 24.3s left on his clock.
winner.why: Second-best score of November (67.2) among 60 blunder-free wins from Nov 2 to Nov 21. The top score (67.6, Nov 17) is this week's Game of the Week, so it is not repeated here. It was the Game of the Week for Nov 10 to Nov 16.

runner_up.caption: 1-minute bullet as White against a 1616, out of the Polish (1.b4). 12.Nxd6+ forked the king and the b7 bishop, 13.Nxb7 cashed in, and after the queens came off he hunted the king to h5 with his pawns: 39.g5+ Kh5 40.Ng7# is mate. No blunders on our Stockfish pass, 94.0 accuracy and 9.4s left on his clock.
runner_up.why: Next in line (63.6). The 64.0 Nov 10 win ranks above it on score but was decided by an opponent error on move 3, so it was passed over, as before. It was the Game of the Week for Nov 3 to Nov 9.

year.label: Game of the Year
year.window_note: Winner unchanged. No November win beats its 68.8 (best: 67.6 on Nov 17).

winner.caption: His best-played game of 2026: as Black in 10-minute rapid against a 2131, 98.5 accuracy, ACPL 10.3 and not even an inaccuracy. He took over after 12...Nd5, won the d-file and queened a pawn before his opponent resigned on move 49.
winner.reason: Beat a 2131 (he was 2068) by resignation after 49...Qxh4 with 98.5 accuracy / 10.3 ACPL and no blunders (Lichess 600+0)
winner.why: It is the only eligible 2026 win over a 2100+ opponent (the next highest is 1990). It has the year's highest accuracy (98.5), full ACPL points (10.3) and a perfect 8/8 clean score, and its opponent-strength score of 12.2 is second only to 12.7. The runner-up (67.2) has the edge on contest and mate, but it beat a 1665 and scored only 1 clean point. The next candidates, #3 (66.1) and #4 (65.9), are bullet wins over opponents rated 1469 and 1574.
winner.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
winner.standout_why: punished the opponent's previous move, eval +0.47→+2.78

runner_up.caption: Seventy-one moves of 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1665, with no blunders and only one mistake: level until move 37, then he out-ground the rook endgame, promoted on h1 and mated with 71...Ra5# with about 3 seconds left.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1665 (he was 1653) by mate (71...Ra5#) with 94.3 accuracy / 16.9 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Unchanged (67.2). The Nov 17 Game of the Week scores 67.6 and would rank second for the year, and the Nov 10 Game of the Month ties at 67.2, but both already fill a slot on the page, so the Sep 23 rook-endgame mate keeps the Year runner-up spot.
runner_up.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
runner_up.standout_why: engine's top move; punished the opponent's previous move, eval +6.77→+10.00
